reviewer_statement: Provisional developer-reviewed source scientific graphics geometry on actual native R sparse joint PACE models, verified in committed tests against exact Matplotlib 1.2 data/artists (not observed green yet). R base graphics is not Matplotlib and runtime plotting return types, colors and injected axes remain outside the accepted scoped scientific domain. No independent certification.
native_language_semantic_policy: Native R scientific artist geometry implements source line/image/scatter coordinates, layout, common color limits, titles, labels and failure markers. The renderer uses R base graphics and cannot return actual Python Matplotlib axes or guarantee pixel-identical output; its typed plot metadata explicitly reports matplotlib_object_identity=false.

case_evidence.description: Frozen Python public src/eyetrajectoriespy/sparse_multivariate_plotting.py::plot_sparse_mfpca_component. Bivariate sparse joint-PACE mean and plus/minus principal-component deviation artist geometry

Real fitted native paired sparse multivariate Gaussian PACE scientific result class, zero-based integer retained component, positive finite SD multiplier. The default native plotting return remains a two-coordinate line data frame collection. strict_source_record=TRUE returns source scientific two-panel artist geometry; Python Matplotlib axes injection is not supported by native R.

Component 0/1+ actual native covariance eigenspectrum controls source lines center(t), center+sd_multiplier*sqrt(lambda_k)*phi_k(t), center-sd_multiplier*sqrt(lambda_k)*phi_k(t). Native source R strict record stores six exact line arrays, labels, titles, x/y axes and legend. Frozen Python 1.2 Matplotlib oracle calls the public plot on the exact same native science object mapped into SparseMFPCAResult and compares each get_ydata and text artist. Existing source scientific test compares population fit arrays directly to Python 1.2. Exact-head CI not yet witnessed green.

Refuses non-native strict result class, invalid zero-based component, nonpositive or nonfinite SD, malformed scientific mean/eigenfunction arrays and missing names; Python exception classes and Matplotlib axes handling are not reproduced.

Source Python returns two Matplotlib Axes instances via NumPy ndarray; native R returns a typed two-panel source-scientific geometry record plus actual native base graphics. Metadata labels and line coordinates are source-aligned, but R is not a Matplotlib renderer and does not return Python Axes class identity.

Visualize retained sparse paired multivariate PACE functional principal direction in both coordinates, reusing the exact fitted mean, eigenvalue and eigenfunction rather than resmoothing or fitting marginal independent models.

independent_review_status: Scoped developer review only; exact-head CI and pinned Matplotlib differential are queued or unverified, no independent scientific contract certification.
language_specific_limits: Matplotlib Axes and Figure identity, external axes injection, and pixel-exact `coolwarm` rendering cannot be implemented by a native base-R graphics return.
Accepted source parity is restricted to fitted scientific array values, line/scatter points, image extents/color limits, metadata and failure geometry, not complete Python graphics objects.
Native result remains a real fitted R scientific object; Python class identity and exact error classes are not interchangeable.
No green exact-head CI observed, independent certification, main-branch merge, or CRAN readiness is claimed.
